Intended design: `audiobooks-auth create` prints the freshly generated TOTP secret once, to the operator's terminal via print(), so it can be entered into the authenticator; enrolment is impossible without disclosing the shared secret at generation time. Not written to any log file (generated at 132, shown only inside the TOTP branch at 150).
Same one-time enrolment output: the otpauth:// URI (153) is the QR-code form of the same secret.

`audiobooks-auth reset-totp` generates a NEW secret (377), invalidates all sessions (383) and prints the new secret once for the operator to hand to the user (393). Same one-time enrolment design as create.
otpauth:// URI form of the same new secret from 388; one-time operator output.

Target host/port are fixed: HTTPConnection('127.0.0.1', API_PORT) at https_server.py:90; only self.path is forwarded, and it must start with '/auth' or '/api' (API_PREFIXES line 31, enforced by _is_api_request line 80). Verified in this venv (Python 3.14.7): http.client.putrequest raises InvalidURL for a path containing CR/LF or a space.

Header key/value come from the backend response (fixed localhost target, line 90), not the request. http.client.parse_headers is line-based and can only yield obs-folded values, never a bare split; the backend is gunicorn, which rejects control chars in response headers (gunicorn/http/wsgi.py HEADER_VALUE_RE) and Werkzeug raises on newline in header values. Covers both the key and value sinks CodeQL reports on this line.

Explicit sanitizer directly above the sink: https_server.py:161-162 strip \r, \n and \0 from host and path before the Location header is built (164). Load-bearing: http.server.send_header accepts a CRLF value unchanged in Python 3.14.7 — do not remove the strip on the assumption the stdlib covers it.
Same explicit sanitizer: redirect_server.py:44-45 strip \r, \n and \0 from host and path before the Location header is built (47).

`if (token)` only chooses between auto-submitting the URL token and showing the manual-entry form; it gates nothing the server does not enforce. POST /auth/magic-link/verify (auth_recovery.py:395-396) independently requires a token (418-420), looks it up (427-429, 400 on miss), rejects expired (431-432) and used (434-435) tokens before any session is created (453).

fixed.reason: Real and severe: measured 40,000 '<' = 5.2 s, 80,000 '<' = 20.7 s (quadratic) on a body whose length cap (line 161) is applied AFTER sanitisation. Regex rewritten <[^>]*?> -> <[^<>]*> (0.9 ms at 80,000). Identical on well-formed input; a literal '<' survives on malformed nesting and the admin UI renders via textContent (suggestions-admin.js:94).

Same sink block as 328 (VERSION .exists() followed symlinks out of the directory); code removed, strict validator rejects a VERSION symlink whose resolve().parent != project dir.

Path(project_path).resolve() ran BEFORE the NUL/'..' guard; pathlib raises ValueError on an embedded NUL, so the guard was dead for exactly the input it exists for and start_upgrade returned an unhandled 500 instead of 400. Guard moved ahead of resolve().

os.path.realpath(user_path) at 904 raises ValueError on an embedded NUL, so the NUL guard at 905 could never fire — GET /api/system/projects?base_path=%00 escaped as an unhandled exception. NUL check moved ahead of realpath().

debug=True was armed by FLASK_DEBUG alone, a generic Flask variable any environment can carry. _debug_enabled() now requires the project's explicit dev switch AUDIOBOOKS_DEV_MODE AND FLASK_DEBUG. Production (gunicorn api_server:app) never executes the __main__ block regardless.
